For the stationary pion, momentum conservation requires the muon and neutrino to have equal and opposite momenta. Treating the neutrino as massless,

\[
E_\nu=\frac{m_\pi^2-m_\mu^2}{2m_\pi}
=\frac{139.6^2-105.7^2}{2(139.6)}
\approx 29.8\ \text{MeV}.
\]

Thus the neutrino’s kinetic energy is \(29.8\) MeV. The total available kinetic energy is

\[
Q=m_\pi-m_\mu=139.6-105.7=33.9\ \text{MeV}.
\]

Therefore, the muon’s kinetic energy is

\[
K_\mu=33.9-29.8\approx4.12\ \text{MeV}.
\]

So \(K_\mu=4.12\) MeV and \(K_\nu=29.8\) MeV; the total should not be doubled.

Answer: A
